reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) describes tribo-oxidation and self-lubricating mechanisms in different alloy systems (CoCrFeNiMo, TiNbZrAg), but none provides specific prior evidence for laser remelting of CoCrFeNi to create a pre-formed graded oxide layer, nor for its performance across the claimed temperature range. The key premises about the intervention and its outcomes are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Laser remelting can induce a finely graded oxide layer on CoCrFeNi
A pre-formed graded oxide layer can act as a lubricious barrier and reduce friction and wear
The oxide layer can accommodate thermal expansion mismatches and resist spallation from RT to 800 °C
The intervention will yield ~25% reduction in friction and notable decrease in wear rate across the full temperature range
